name: Recover lost backlinks with DataForSEO, OpenAI, Google Sheets and Slack

parameters.content:
## Recover the backlinks you lost, worst first

Put your domain in `Settings`. Every Monday this pulls the links that died recently, works out *why* each one died, and sorts them into what you can fix yourself and what needs an email.

### How it works

`backlinks_status_type` is set to `lost`, not a filter on `is_lost` - the filter form answers `20000 Ok.` with zero rows. A `last_seen` window turns 51,163 archived losses into the 9,053 that actually died recently.

Each loss is then sorted by what the row says about it. Your page returning 404 is not outreach, it is a redirect you owe yourself. Their page returning 404 is not recoverable at all. Only a link that vanished while both pages stayed healthy is worth writing to somebody about, and that is the only bucket the model drafts an angle for.

Your own page is re-checked live first, because the status code on the row is from whenever DataForSEO last crawled it.

### Setup

Add an **HTTP Basic Auth** credential holding your DataForSEO login and password, then open `Settings` and put in your domain. Point the Google Sheet and Slack channel wherever you want them.

Create a Data Table called `lost_link_watch` with three text columns - `link_id`, `bucket` and `seen_on` - so a link you already worked is not handed to you again next week.

## 1. Which domain, and how far back
`lost_since_days` is what turns an archive into a work queue. n8n.io has 51,163 lost links on record and 9,053 that died in the last six weeks.

## 2. Ask for lost, do not filter for it
`backlinks_status_type` set to `lost` is the parameter that works. A filter on `is_lost` answers 20000 Ok with zero rows.

## 3. One conversation per domain
A domain that linked from forty pages is one email, not forty. Links you already worked are dropped here.

## 4. Check your own side first
The status code on the row is from DataForSEO's last crawl. Whether your page serves a 404 right now decides whether this is outreach or a redirect you owe yourself.

## 5. Only removals need an email
The model writes an angle for one bucket: links that vanished while both pages stayed healthy.

## 6. The sheet and the watch list
Both hang off the report, never behind it. A Sheets append emits the row it wrote and a Data Table write emits the row it stored.

## 7. Or the quiet version
A week with nothing new still posts, so silence always means the workflow did not run.

## 8. When it breaks
An Error Trigger is a separate entry point, so a failed run says so in Slack instead of going quiet.

## Check your own side first

A 404 on your page is the row's most valuable state and the cheapest to act on. It is re-checked live here because the code on the row is from DataForSEO's last crawl, not from now.

parameters.text:
=You are writing the first line of a link recovery email. Below are links to {{ $('Settings').first().json.domain }} that were removed while both the linking page and the linked page are still healthy.

{{ $json.outreach_brief }}

For each numbered item, write one sentence a human could send: what the page was about, and why re-adding the link helps their reader. Do not invent facts about either page beyond what is given. Do not write a greeting or a signature.
Answer as numbered lines matching the numbers above, nothing else. If an item gives you nothing to work with, write that number followed by 'no angle from the data'.

=*Lost backlinks for {{ $('Settings').first().json.domain }}*
{{ $('Drop The Ones We Sent').first().json.failed
  ? 'The API call did not come back clean: ' + $('Drop The Ones We Sent').first().json.reason
  : 'Nothing new. Every recent loss on record has already been triaged and logged.' }}
